title: access-review-evidence-automation-and-siem-mapping-notes
content:
Purpose:
Collect notes for automating evidence collection for quarterly least-privilege recertification and mapping audit logs to SIEM. These are working notes for the RBAC v2 migration and the access-review automation sprint.

Scope:
- Privileged roles: infra-admin, ded-cluster-admin, console-ops, secret-approver, billing-admin (first pass).
- Systems: Redwood Console (authz service), IAM service (RBAC v2), Audit Log pipeline (Kafka -> S3 -> Lakehouse), SIEM endpoints (Splunk/Datadog ingest).
- Deliverables: evidence bundle format, SIEM field mapping, automation runbook for quarterly recert.

Background / Why this matters (quick):
- We need auditable, reproducible evidence for enterprise SOC/ISO audits showing recertification decisions and role justifications.
- RBAC v2 adds role-conditions and resource-scoped grants which complicates simple "role membership" exports. Evidence must capture effective permissions (including policy conditions) at time-of-review.

Current gaps identified:
- Audit log schema is inconsistent across services; some events missing resource_arn and session_id.
- Manual exports used to collect reviewer evidence; time-consuming and error-prone.
- SIEM ingest expects flat fields; our current audit JSON has nested arrays (grants[], conditions[]).
- No canonical evidence bundle format for access-review artifacts (who approved, timestamp, justification, snapshot of effective perms).

High-level proposal:
1) Standardize audit log schema across services (minimal required fields).
   - event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, resource_arn, grant_type, grant_id, grant_source, effective_permissions (comma-separated), session_id, request_id, trace_id, outcome, metadata_url
2) Add an "effective_permissions_snapshot_url" field that points to an immutable S3 object containing a flattened CSV of perms for that subject at that timestamp (helps RBAC v2 conditions).
3) Evidence bundle format (JSONL): header record (review_id, reviewer, reviewed_at, window_start, window_end, rationale_link), then records for each privileged user/role containing: subject_id, current_roles, effective_permissions_s3_url, last_activity_ts, linked_jira_ids, decision (keep/remove/modify), approver_id, approver_note.
4) Automation flow: nightly job generates permission snapshots for all privileged roles and writes audit events to Kafka with audit schema; nightly exporter writes SIEM-mapped events to Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) and Datadog logs endpoint.

Audit log -> SIEM field mapping (draft):
- event_id -> id
- timestamp_utc -> _time
- actor_id -> user.id
- actor_email -> user.email
- action -> event.action
- resource_type/resource_id/resource_arn -> resource.type / resource.id / resource.arn (flattened)
- grant_type/grant_id/grant_source -> grant.type / grant.id / grant.source
- effective_permissions -> event.effective_permissions (csv string)
- session_id / request_id / trace_id -> session.id / request.id / trace.id
- outcome -> event.outcome
- metadata_url -> event.meta_url (used to fetch full context in long-term storage)

Notes on nested fields: we will stringify nested arrays as JSON string OR create a flattened CSV for the most important one (effective_permissions). Preference: put both a flattened csv field and a metadata_url for the full object to avoid losing searchable tokens.

Evidence packaging and retention:
- Evidence bundles for each quarterly review must be immutable and stored for minimum 2 years (per compliance ask). Storage: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/recert/{{year}}/q{{quarter}}/{{review_id}}.zip (encrypted with KMS: awskms://alias/redwood-compliance-kms).
- Bundle components: human-readable summary (md), machine-parseable JSONL snapshot, raw audit events (JSONL), review decisions CSV, signer logs (cloudkms signature or SA key id).
- Retention policy: 2 years active, then archived to Glacier Flexible Retrieval for 5 years.

Recertification cadence & playbook (working):
- Pre-window (T-14 to T-7 days): automation job publishes "candidate list" of privileged accounts (based on role tag privileged=true and last_activity within 12 months). Slack announce to security-ops and product-owners.
- Review window (T-7 to T+7 days): reviewers get secure link to the evidence bundle. Reviewer flow in Console: accept/decline/propose-change + freeform justification. All responses generate an audit event and are captured in review decision CSV.
- Post-window (T+8 to T+14): auto-enforce changes for "remove" decisions if not appealed. Enforcement runs under change freeze windows and emits remediation audit events.

Risk scoring / sampling heuristic (for large orgs):
- Score each subject by: (role_risk_weight * number_of_privileged_roles) + (1.0 if last_activity < 90d) + (2.0 if role_grants_sensitive_resource) + (1.5 if external_identity_source) + (0.5 if MFA missing).
- Recertify all > threshold, sample 20% of medium risk for deeper evidence collection.

RBAC v2 specifics to capture in evidence snapshot:
- Explicit grants vs inherited grants (explicit/inherited flag)
- Condition expressions (e.g., resource.name == "prod-*" OR request.ip in CIDR) must be rendered into human-readable summary and stored in the full metadata_url object.
- Time-limited grants: include grant_expires_at, grant_issued_by, and original_request_id.

Operational runbook (short):
- Run nightly snapshot job: infra/team -> cron job "rbac-snapshot" (k8s cronjob) writes to s3 and emits event: event.action = "rbac.snapshot".
- Run pre-window candidate exporter: script exports candidate list, creates review_id and creates evidence bundle placeholder (marked pending).
- Kick reviewers: create secure ephemeral links (signed URL TTL 7d).
- After reviewer decisions, run enforcement pipeline with safety checks and manual gate for high-risk (> 8) users.

Metrics to track (visibility in Console):
- % of privileged accounts reviewed each quarter
- Avg time to reviewer decision
- % of auto-enforcements executed without rollback
- Number of SIEM alerts tied to recert events (new)

Open questions / blockers (capture for next sync):
- Who owns the canonical role risk weights? (security + product owners?)
- Need decision on flattening vs keeping nested for SIEM indexing cost (splunk ingestion cost vs usefulness).
- Legal wants chain-of-approval stored as signed artifact; do we use KMS signing or a dedicated signing service?
- Some services cannot yet emit resource_arn; need priority list to fix SDKs.

Action items (owners):
- Evan Morales: implement audit-schema change in authz service (PR + migration plan) - target: 2026-03-24. (JIRA-SEC-4321)
- Jules Park: prototype SIEM mapping lambda that transforms audit events and posts to Splunk HEC - target: 2026-03-17.
- Marta Kowalski: draft evidence bundle JSONL schema and example for Legal review - target: 2026-03-05 (blocker: legal comment pending).
- Priya Nair (owner): coordinate cross-team rollouts, create runbook draft and schedule table-top recert simulation - target: 2026-03-31.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep evidence size reasonable: snapshots should be deltas for less-churn accounts.
- Consider signing each evidence bundle with a delegated service account to make chain-of-custody easy to validate.
- For export performance: batch SIEM pushes hourly and use bulk endpoints.

References / links to prototypes: 
- example evidence bundle (prototype): s3://redwood-compliance/prototypes/evidence-demo.jsonl
- SIEM mapping lambda skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-tools/tree/main/siem-mapper
- Confluence design page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design (see section: "Audit schema v1.1")

Meeting notes / decisions log (append here after each sync):
- 2026-02-20: agreed to two-field approach for perms: flattened_csv + metadata_url (Evan/Jules/Marta)
- 2026-02-28: legal asked for 2-year accessible retention and signature; proposing KMS-signed manifest (open)

Unresolved / parking lot items:
- How to represent cross-account roles for partner integrations (partner_id field?)
- Backfill policy: do we retroactively snapshot prior months or only start at go-live?

Next steps before next sync (Priya):
1) Lock schema PR and get approval from infra/product owners.
2) Run small-scale evidence generation for 50 users and push to Splunk sandbox.
3) Draft reviewer UX copy and Slack templates for T-14 announce.

If you want to play with the sample CLI: 
- ./scripts/generate_evidence --review-id demo-2026q1 --output s3://redwood-compliance/prototypes/ 

Comments welcome in-thread or drop quick reactions in #Sec-Access-Reviews.

-- Priya
